## Pull request overview

Adds schema-level export configuration and UI support so `ObjectGrid` can export visible data to CSV/JSON, and updates the console roadmap to reflect Phase 10 (L1) completion.

**Changes:**
- Added `ObjectGridSchema.exportOptions` (mirrors `ListViewSchema.exportOptions`) to configure export formats and limits.
- Implemented an Export popover in `ObjectGrid` that downloads CSV/JSON when enabled via `schema.exportOptions`.
- Added a new grid export test suite and updated `ROADMAP_CONSOLE.md` progress/status sections.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 4 out of 4 changed files in this pull request and generated 8 comments.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/types/src/objectql.ts | Extends `ObjectGridSchema` with `exportOptions` configuration. |
| packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx | Adds export popover UI and CSV/JSON download implementation gated by `exportOptions`. |
| packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/grid-export.test.tsx | Adds tests for Export button rendering and default formats behavior. |
| ROADMAP_CONSOLE.md | Updates roadmap statuses to mark Phase 10 L1 complete and adjusts milestone/status text. |

Export uses the raw `data` state and does not reflect client-side table state (search filtering / interactive sorting / pagination) handled inside the `data-table` renderer. This can produce exports that don’t match what the user is currently viewing. Consider exporting the same filtered/sorted dataset the table is rendering (e.g., by delegating export to the data-table layer or lifting the visible rows state up).

The Export button’s visible label is hidden on small screens (`hidden sm:inline`), which can leave the trigger without an accessible name in mobile layouts. Add an `aria-label` (or an `sr-only` label) so screen readers and voice control can identify the button even when the text is visually hidden.

`(schema.exportOptions.formats || ['csv', 'json']).map(format => ...)` will infer `format` as `string` because the fallback array is `string[]`, but `handleExport` expects the `'csv' | 'xlsx' | 'json' | 'pdf'` union. This is likely to fail TypeScript type-checking. Use a const-typed default (or otherwise narrow/cast) so `format` stays within the expected union.

On small screens `useCardView` returns early before `exportToolbar` is created/rendered, so `exportOptions` has no effect on mobile card view. If export should be available on mobile too, render the toolbar in the card-view branch (or move its definition above the early return).

`ObjectGridSchema.exportOptions` duplicates the exact same inline shape already defined for `ListViewSchema.exportOptions` in this file. Consider extracting a shared `ExportOptions` type alias to keep the two schemas in lockstep and avoid future drift.

New `exportOptions` fields (`maxRecords`, `includeHeaders`, `fileNamePrefix`) are exercised by the implementation, but the tests only cover button visibility and default formats. Add assertions around these options (and ideally that selecting a format triggers a download) to ensure the behavior doesn’t regress.

`handleExport` accepts/advertises xlsx/pdf, and the toolbar will render those formats if configured, but the implementation only handles csv/json (xlsx/pdf clicks become no-ops). Either implement the additional formats or filter/disable unsupported formats (and consider surfacing an error/toast when a format isn’t supported).
